chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from more than one, from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl, said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who rented land from another man, and he said: 'I rented it to you for such and such an amount; if I cultivate it, [I keep the rent], and if I do not cultivate it, I will give you that [amount].' He did not cultivate it. He (the Imam) said: 'He has the right to take [the rent]; if he wishes, he leaves it [unpaid/withholds it], and if he wishes, he does not leave it [i.e., he takes it].'

key_terms.لَمْ يَتْرُكْهُ: he did not leave it (took the right/payment)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a tenant rents land for cultivation but does not farm it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of *muzara'ah* contracts, granting the landlord discretion to enforce the fixed rent or waive it if the tenant fails to cultivate the land. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on contractual fairness and the landlord's right to choose the most equitable outcome, reflecting the practical application of Islamic commercial law in agrarian societies. The hadith underscores the principle that such agreements are binding yet allow for judicial or mutual discretion in cases of non-performance.
